problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,1,-5)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Cartesian Equation of a Plane

feedback.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $5y-z+17=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨0,5,-1⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-z+17 & =0 \\ z & =5y+17.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=17.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,17)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,17⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,17⟩)\cdot ⟨0,5,-1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
